cells.tense: You are standing here with all of it felt at once, not a piece missing.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about where this connection stands and where it doesn't, unhurried, and let the second half stand.
cells.core:
You feel the whole thing at once - what you owe them, what they owe you, what you would do again - and it holds together as one piece you don't have to keep sorting.

Someone speaks and it lands, and you stay steady while it lands. You don't audit the relationship or defend a version of it. You know it. That steadiness isn't distance; nothing here needs managing right now. Closeness comes and goes at its real size. The invitation is small and easy to take: let one exchange today be exactly as close as it actually is, no more and no less.
cells.sheetLine: You know what this connection is, and you're not straining to hold it.
cells.verb: knowing what you feel for someone all the way through
cells.place: in the moment what you are stops asking permission to show

cells.tense: You are trying to feel the whole thing finished before it has finished being felt.
cells.ask: Name one thing about this connection that isn't yours to decide yet, and leave it named and unresolved.
cells.core:
You want the ending before it's here. Somewhere ahead the feeling is supposed to be complete and calm, and you're rehearsing that calm now - deciding how it goes, deciding what it meant, closing it early so it can't surprise you. The bracing feels like care. It's actually you running the whole film instead of watching it.

Something alive here goes quiet the moment it's declared finished. What it costs you is the part that hasn't happened yet, and that part is the only part that could still be given to you. Let one thing about this stay undecided today. Not forever. Just today.

cells.tense: You decided not to feel this whole thing, and you have been standing there since.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you care about here - a message, a call, a door held - and act before you feel ready.
cells.core:
The feeling is whole. What dropped out is you. The full size of what you'd feel for someone got narrowed down to what you'd let through, and now the connections in front of you get an edited version - and often you aren't inside them at all.

Not much is needed. A spark, not a plan - do one small thing that shows someone you're here, and let the doing carry you into the room. The size of the feeling doesn't have to arrive first. Presence is the whole ask. It usually shows up about ten seconds after the action, not before.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting the whole feeling through, and you're still stopped.

cells.tense: You are already choosing what is fair in this connection while calling it common sense.
cells.ask: For one thing you did today, say plainly to yourself that you did it because it was right, not because it was on the way.
cells.core:
You keep a running sense of what's owed in the connections around you - who has been met fairly, who hasn't. When it's working well this is a light hand: you give and take without keeping notes, the sense of what's right arrives clean, and you move on it. Nothing to tabulate. You just know.

What's happening now is that the same sense runs constantly and gets folded into common sense. But that is you setting the terms. The terms are already authored. The sign-off isn't. When you weigh what someone deserves, notice it's a weigh and not an instinct - you are deciding. Saying so to yourself makes what you give yours instead of automatic, and it steadies how you give. Nothing to fix. Something to sign.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the score in this connection. Call it yours.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person has ever felt whole or ever lost it, so the too much and too little cores locate a completed emotional knowing only through how they're handling it now, not through a history. The reader could reasonably object that they already know how they feel and don't need a stranger naming it, which is why every cell hands the act back and never grades the state. The ask survives being wrong: saying one true sentence about where this connection stands and where it doesn't is useful whether or not the card seats them. The line that serves me is 'the wholeness is already yours' — it flatters the reading, so it's out.
